title: Choose DUMA’s new visual world
question: The current instrument-like system is being replaced. Choose the friendlier world that should govern the app, or re-roll.

options.label: The Service Board
options.lineage: café prep walls, magnetic rota boards, and colour-coded service passes
options.thesis: One shared board reshaped around each role, with warm modular surfaces and colour that carries ownership and priority.
options.viewport: A calm coloured sidebar opens onto a daily operating board, with primary work grouped into soft modules and urgent work pinned visibly rather than buried in tabs.
options.risk: Too many coloured modules could feel juvenile, so colour belongs to product domains and state—not decoration.

options.label: Depth Bands
options.lineage: a technical dive through changing light and depth
options.thesis: The app moves from bright shop-floor actions into deeper layers of management and group control.
options.case: Strong colour and hierarchy, but the ocean metaphor identifies less immediately with café operators than the service board.
options.viewport: A light cyan action layer sits above progressively deeper blue management bands, with the current role fixing the visible depth.
options.risk: The vertical metaphor may become decorative on dense tables and repetitive operational pages.

options.label: Role Stacks
options.lineage: HyperCard stacks and editable index cards
options.thesis: Every role receives a linked stack of task cards, with browse and edit treated as two modes of the same object.
options.case: Excellent task clarity and familiarity, but its monochrome source fuses poorly with the explicit request for more colour.
options.viewport: A compact role stack uses visible back paths, direct-edit fields, and a single coloured selection layer.
options.risk: Pixel nostalgia could make the product feel older—the exact problem this redesign must remove.

options.label: Safelight Workflow
options.lineage: darkroom stations and timed process baths
options.thesis: Complex work advances through visible stations, previews, and deliberate commit points.
options.case: Its workflow grammar is strong, but amber-on-dark feels too severe for a shared tablet used all day.
options.viewport: The current task is a bright station inside a dark process line, with test states shown before irreversible actions.
options.risk: The dark environment would increase glare and make routine screens feel more dramatic than the work warrants.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished contemporary SaaS admin system with a soft neutral canvas, indigo accent, rounded cards, and familiar sidebar navigation.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional sidebar, metric cards, activity table, and primary action arranged exactly where an experienced admin user expects them.
canonCard.risk: Highly usable, but likely to retain the generic AI-dashboard feeling the brief explicitly rejects.
